criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Identifies overbroad MAE carve-outs for environmental industry/regulations
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies the MAE carve-outs for conditions generally affecting the environmental services industry and changes in Environmental Laws as problematic because they lack a disproportionate-impact exception, and it proposes adding such a qualifier.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Proposes adding disproportionate impact qualifier to MAE carve-outs
criteria_results.reasoning: The proposed MAE definition expressly adds a disproportionate-impact exception for the general carve-outs and specifically states that industry and Environmental Law changes are taken into account when they disproportionately affect the Company relative to other environmental services industry participants.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Provides actual revised contract language for MAE definition
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum includes a full draft-ready replacement MAE definition and expressly provides that specified carve-outs are taken into account to the extent they disproportionately affect the Company relative to other industry participants.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Explains rationale — environmental company needs MAE protection
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly explains that Cascadia's value is directly exposed to environmental regulation and industry economics, so carve-outs for environmental-services industry conditions and Environmental Law changes could remove the very risks the MAE provision is intended to cover. It further notes that the qualifier is especially important given the target's environmental permits, government contracts, and CERCLA exposure.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Identifies missing interim covenant restricting affiliate transactions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the interim covenant omits restrictions on transactions with Seller and Seller affiliates, and proposes a buyer-consent restriction covering entry into, amendment, renewal, payment under, and termination of affiliate arrangements between signing and closing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Proposes covenant requiring Buyer consent for affiliate transactions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum proposes a new Section 6.01(b)(xiv) prohibiting the Company from entering into, amending, modifying, extending, renewing, supplementing, altering, or terminating transactions or agreements with Seller or its affiliates without Buyer's prior written consent.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: References the above-market rent to Seller affiliate as rationale
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly ties the affiliate-transaction covenant to the Company’s $1,600,000 annual rent under a Seller-affiliate lease and further identifies the above-market rent adjustment as supporting the covenant.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Identifies indemnification cap discrepancy (20% vs. 12.5%)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the Seller draft uses a 20% general indemnification cap of $43,000,000, while the executed term sheet requires a 12.5% cap of $26,875,000, and provides conforming replacement language.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Proposes redline reducing cap to 12.5% / $26,875,000
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly proposes replacing the indemnification cap with $26,875,000, equal to 12.5% of the $215,000,000 Base Enterprise Value, in both the definition and Section 9.04(b).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: References the term sheet as basis for cap correction
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly cites the executed term sheet in the indemnification-cap section, stating that Term Sheet §8 fixes the general cap at 12.5% of the $215 million Base Enterprise Value, or $26.875 million.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Identifies that environmental reps survival period is too short
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the Seller's draft gives all non-fundamental representations, including environmental representations, only 12 months of survival and states that this is inadequate for environmental compliance, permit, remediation, CERCLA, and delayed regulatory risks. It proposes a separate 36-month survival period for Environmental Representations, expressly including Section 4.15 and Environmental Permits.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Proposes extending environmental reps survival to at least 36 months
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly proposes that Environmental Representations survive until 36 months after closing and also notes the option of seeking survival through the full applicable statute of limitations.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: References CERCLA/Dalton Creek exposure as rationale for longer survival
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly connects longer environmental-representation survival to Dalton Creek CERCLA exposure and active remediation. It states that 12 months is inadequate because of Dalton Creek, the 24–36 month Hargrove project, delayed regulatory action, and CERCLA matters that can take years to crystallize, supporting the proposed 36-month survival period.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Identifies anti-sandbagging provision in Section 9.06
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies Section 9.06 as an anti-sandbagging provision and quotes its language barring Buyer from indemnification for breaches or inaccuracies known by Buyer or its Representatives as of the Closing Date.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Proposes replacing with pro-sandbagging language
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly deletes the anti-sandbagging provision and replaces it with a pro-sandbagging clause stating that Buyer's indemnification and other remedies are not affected, limited, diminished, or impaired by any investigation or knowledge acquired before or after execution or Closing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Provides actual pro-sandbagging contract text
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum includes actual proposed pro-sandbagging contract language in replacement Section 9.06, expressly providing that Buyer's indemnification and other remedies are not affected by its investigation, knowledge, notice, or available information.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Identifies need for Special Indemnity for Dalton Creek CERCLA matter
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly proposes a separate “Dalton Creek Special Indemnity” for the EPA Section 104(e)/CERCLA matter, distinct from general environmental representations and general indemnification. It also specifies separate survival, basket, cap, and escrow treatment.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Special Indemnity survival of 72 months
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states that the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity “shall survive the Closing until the date that is seventy-two (72) months after the Closing Date,” satisfying the required six-year post-closing survival period.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Special Indemnity not subject to basket or cap
criteria_results.reasoning: The Dalton Creek Special Indemnity provision expressly states that it “shall not be subject to the Basket Amount, the Indemnification Cap, or any other general limitation,” and further clarifies that related losses do not count toward the basket or reduce the general cap.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: References Dalton Creek liability range ($1.5M-$6M)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states in the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity issue summary that the DD memo estimates potential CERCLA liability of $1,500,000 to $6,000,000, using that exposure to justify the Special Indemnity.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Identifies problematic earnout operational covenant
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies Section 2.05(d) as imposing an overly restrictive affirmative obligation to operate consistently with past practice, act in good faith to maximize the earnout, maintain resources, and avoid diversion of opportunities. It recommends replacing that covenant with a narrow primary-purpose negative covenant.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Proposes limiting earnout covenant to no-frustration standard
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly replaces the affirmative past-practice and earnout-maximization obligations with a narrow covenant prohibiting actions taken with the primary purpose of reducing or avoiding the earnout payment, while preserving Buyer's operational discretion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Explains rationale — Buyer integration/restructuring flexibility
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly explains that the seller’s broad earnout covenant would give Seller a de facto veto over Buyer’s platform integration, bolt-on acquisitions, restructuring, and operational improvements. It also proposes language preserving Buyer’s discretion to integrate, restructure, and otherwise manage the Company, directly addressing the commercial risk to post-closing operational freedom.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Identifies missing payoff letter requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the Seller draft permits repayment “at or promptly following” closing and lacks a payoff-letter condition, then proposes requiring executed payoff letters from each holder at least three business days before closing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Proposes payoff letters at least 3 business days pre-closing
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly requires executed payoff letters to be delivered no later than three business days before closing, and requires each letter to include wiring instructions and provide for lien releases, including UCC termination statements and other lien-release documents.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Proposes simultaneous repayment at closing through funds flow
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly replaces the seller's “at or promptly following” mechanic with a requirement that all Closing Indebtedness be repaid simultaneously at Closing through the closing funds flow, including direct wires to the applicable debt holders.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Proposes payoff letter delivery as a condition to closing
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly proposes adding Section 7.02(i), requiring Buyer to receive executed payoff letters at least three Business Days before closing and stating that delivery is a condition to Buyer's obligation to close.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Identifies missing government contract anti-assignment/novation requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the Seller's draft does not address government-contract anti-assignment, novation, or recognition requirements for the Oregon DEQ, Washington Ecology, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, and Bureau of Land Management contracts. It specifically discusses the Anti-Assignment Act and FAR Part 42, Subpart 42.12, and proposes related representations, covenants, and closing conditions.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: References specific government contracts requiring novation
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum specifically lists all four active government contracts and states that the two federal contracts—U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and Bureau of Land Management—require novation analysis under FAR §42.1204.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Proposes closing condition or covenant for government contract novation
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum proposes a specific pre-closing covenant in new Section 6.06A requiring Seller and the Company to notify contracting officers, submit required novation or recognition requests, and use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain the agreements or approvals. It also proposes a related closing condition in Section 7.02(h) requiring submission, no denial or termination indication, and interim-performance confirmation if final novation is pending.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: References Anti-Assignment Act or FAR provisions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly cites the federal Anti-Assignment Act, 41 U.S.C. § 6305, and FAR Part 42, Subpart 42.12, including FAR § 42.1204, as the legal basis for government-contract novation or recognition requirements.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Identifies missing environmental permit transfer/notification covenant
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the Seller draft represents the Company holds 23 environmental permits but lacks covenants requiring identification of change-of-control requirements, pre-closing notices or approvals, and post-closing cooperation. It also proposes a detailed Environmental Permit Change-of-Control Cooperation covenant covering transfer, reissuance, amendment, notification, and approval processes.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Proposes cooperation covenant for environmental permit transfers
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly proposes new Section 6.06B requiring Seller and the Company to identify permit change-of-control requirements, prepare and submit pre-closing notifications and approval requests, and provide post-closing cooperation for at least 12 months with permit transfers, reissuances, amendments, notifications, and approvals under applicable state requirements.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Notes that permits may require notification even in a stock deal
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states that “A stock transaction does not eliminate state change-of-control requirements” and discusses notification or approval requirements for environmental permits in Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada, including Oregon DEQ and Washington Ecology.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Identifies missing R&W Insurance subrogation waiver
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the Seller's draft contains no reference to R&W Insurance and no waiver of the insurer's subrogation rights against Seller or related persons, and it proposes draft waiver language.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Proposes subrogation waiver provision with fraud exception
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum proposes a new R&W insurance provision requiring the insurer to irrevocably waive subrogation and other recovery rights against Seller and related persons, with an express exception for losses arising from actual fraud committed by Seller. It also identifies Granite Ridge Underwriters as the contemplated insurer.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: References R&W Insurance policy / Granite Ridge Underwriters
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states that Buyer is obtaining a representations and warranties insurance policy and ties that policy to a required insurer subrogation waiver against Seller, except for Seller fraud. It also identifies the contemplated insurer as Granite Ridge Underwriters in the issue summary and negotiation notes.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Identifies non-compete scope exceeds term sheet (duration)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the Seller draft imposes a five-year non-compete and states that the term sheet requires a three-year restriction, with replacement language conforming the duration to three years.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Identifies non-compete scope exceeds term sheet (geographic)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the Seller draft applies nationwide ('anywhere in the United States') while the term sheet limits the non-compete to Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada, and proposes replacement language using those four states.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Identifies non-compete scope exceeds term sheet (activity)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the Seller's draft applies to “any business” and contrasts it with the term sheet’s narrower scope limited to environmental remediation and hazardous waste management services.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Proposes narrowing non-compete duration to 3 years
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly proposes replacing Section 6.09(a) with a non-compete lasting “three (3) years following the Closing Date,” matching the term sheet.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Proposes narrowing non-compete geographic scope to OR, WA, CA, NV
criteria_results.reasoning: The proposed replacement for Section 6.09(a) expressly limits the non-compete to environmental remediation or hazardous waste management businesses in Oregon, Washington, California, or Nevada, matching the term sheet.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Proposes narrowing non-compete activity scope to environmental remediation and hazardous waste management
criteria_results.reasoning: The proposed replacement for Section 6.09(a) expressly narrows the restricted activity to businesses providing environmental remediation services or hazardous waste management services, matching the term sheet.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Notes enforceability risk of overbroad non-compete
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states that the five-year, nationwide restriction on engaging in “any business” would sweep in Evergreen’s unrelated construction and timber operations and create enforceability risk, including that it could be struck as overbroad.

criteria_results.title: Indemnification cap issue rated as Critical or High priority
criteria_results.reasoning: The indemnification cap discrepancy (20% versus 12.5%) is expressly assigned HIGH priority in both the executive summary and the detailed Article IX discussion.

criteria_results.title: Anti-sandbagging issue rated as Critical or High priority
criteria_results.reasoning: The anti-sandbagging issue in Section 9.06 is expressly labeled “PRIORITY: CRITICAL,” which is the highest priority tier and satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Memorandum identifies provisions acceptable as drafted
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum includes a dedicated “Items Intentionally Not Marked Up” section identifying multiple provisions acceptable as drafted—such as the basket/deductible, knowledge qualifier, good-standing certificates, Delaware governing law, and NWC true-up—and briefly explains their consistency with the term sheet or buyer playbook.

criteria_results.title: Memorandum flags items for partner/client discussion
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly includes a “Client Decisions / Negotiation Notes” section flagging multiple issues for further discussion or confirmation, including government-contract novation timing with Marcus, environmental-representation survival, the Dalton Creek escrow structure, and the R&W insurance closing condition. It also directs Elena to discuss certain positions with Marcus before finalizing the markup.

criteria_results.title: Escrow amount correctly stated as $16,125,000 (7.5% of EV)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum correctly states the escrow amount as $16,125,000 and identifies it as 7.5% of the $215,000,000 base enterprise value in its indemnification and escrow discussions.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Proposes 36-month escrow holdback for Special Indemnity
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly provides that the escrow portion allocated to the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity will be held until 36 months after closing, with unresolved timely claims reserved thereafter. It distinguishes this special-indemnity holdback from the general escrow mechanics.

criteria_results.title: Earnout maximum correctly referenced as $25,000,000
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum correctly states the maximum earnout payment as $25,000,000 in the proposed earnout provision and related commentary.

criteria_results.title: Earnout Adjusted EBITDA threshold correctly referenced as $38,000,000
criteria_results.reasoning: The earnout discussion correctly states that the maximum earnout is payable if Adjusted EBITDA equals or exceeds $38,000,000, and repeatedly identifies $38,000,000 as the full-payment threshold.

criteria_results.title: Earnout floor correctly referenced as $32,000,000
criteria_results.reasoning: The earnout provision correctly states a $32,000,000 floor, provides no payment below that amount, and applies linear pro-rata interpolation between $32,000,000 and the $38,000,000 full-payment threshold.

criteria_results.title: References playbook as authority for at least 3 markup positions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum cites the Buyer M&A Playbook as authority for well over three distinct markup positions, including the MAE definition, earnout covenant, government-contract novation provisions, affiliate-transaction restriction, debt payoff mechanics, environmental survival, pro-sandbagging, and non-compete provisions.

criteria_results.title: References term sheet as authority for at least 3 markup positions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum cites the executed term sheet as authority for well over three distinct markup positions, including earnout mechanics, the indemnification cap, environmental-representation survival, the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, debt payoff mechanics, the R&W insurance subrogation waiver, and the non-compete.

criteria_results.title: References environmental DD memo for at least one markup position
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum repeatedly cites the environmental DD memo as support for markup positions, including government-contract novation, environmental permit transfers, environmental representation survival, and the Dalton Creek special indemnity.

criteria_results.title: Memorandum identifies specific SPA section numbers for issues
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum ties all 12 planted issues to specific SPA sections, including Sections 1.01, 2.05, 4.16, 6.01, 6.05, 6.09, 7.02, 9.01, 9.02, 9.04, 9.06, and 9.08. This exceeds the requirement of at least 8 issues.

criteria_results.title: Proposed redline language is actual contract text for at least 8 issues
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum provides draft-ready contractual language suitable for insertion into the SPA for all 12 principal issues, including the MAE definition, earnout, government contracts, affiliate transactions, debt payoff, environmental permits, indemnification cap, environmental survival, Dalton Creek indemnity, pro-sandbagging, R&W insurance, and non-compete provisions. This exceeds the requirement of at least 8 issues.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Identifies all three sources of Target indebtedness
criteria_results.reasoning: The payoff-letter discussion expressly identifies all three sources of Target indebtedness: Cascade Mutual Bank ($28.0M), Pacific Lease Corp. ($9.8M), and Evergreen Holdings Group, Inc. ($4.5M), and requires payoff letters from each holder.
